I will still plant all 9.0 mu to cotton. On my size of land, one bad cotton year hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer, so I will start from what has worked on the North China Plain and then adjust for my well irrigation and my own yield target. Cotton here cannot be fed only with nitrogen, otherwise it grows too much stalk and drops fruiting, so I will keep nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium in balance. I will use an improved cotton seed, not old saved seed, because stand uniformity and boll setting matter more than saving a little seed money. For tillage, I will plough before sowing because continuous cotton can leave the soil tight, and I want the roots to go down and use the irrigation water better. With well water available, I will plan three irrigations: one around early squaring if the soil is short of moisture, one at flowering and boll setting, and one later if the weather stays dry. For pests, I will not wait until they spread badly; I will budget about five sprays across the season for aphids, bollworm, mites, and late-season sucking pests, because on 9 mu it is better to keep the field clean than lose yield. My target is a steady, saleable crop, not chasing the absolute highest output, so I will aim around 330 kg per mu of seed cotton.
